title: What are the three views of seven solids?
description: Seven solids, a cube, a cuboid, a parallelepiped, a cylinder, a cone, a prism and a pyramid, are each placed on a face or a base. The board looks at each from the front, from above and from the side and names the shape of each view.
teaching_notes: One idea: each view is the outline the eye meets from one direction, so fix the way the solid stands and look three times. Watch for students who give the cone a triangle from above.

source: Figure it Out (views of solids, question 2)
video_script.why: The child finds the three views of each solid by fixing how it stands and looking from the front, from above and from the side, because each view is the outline the eye meets from that direction.
video_script.substitution: cube on a face: three squares; cuboid on a face: three rectangles; parallelepiped leaning forward: parallelogram from the side, rectangles from front and top; cylinder standing: rectangle, circle, rectangle; cone standing: triangle, circle with a dot at the centre, triangle; triangular prism with its triangle facing front: triangle, rectangle, rectangle; square pyramid standing: triangle, square with both diagonals, triangle.
video_script.anchor: the seven solids of the book in a row, each with an eye at the front, above and at the side
video_script.payoff_line: The cube gives squares. The cuboid gives rectangles. The leaning box gives a parallelogram and rectangles. The cylinder gives rectangle, circle, rectangle. The cone gives triangle, circle, triangle. The prism gives a triangle and rectangles. The pyramid gives triangles and a square with diagonals

final_answer.value: Cube: squares; cuboid: rectangles; parallelepiped: parallelogram and rectangles; cylinder: rectangle, circle, rectangle; cone: triangle, circle, triangle; prism: triangle and rectangles; pyramid: triangles and a square with diagonals
final_answer.spoken: cube, squares; cuboid, rectangles; parallelepiped, parallelogram and rectangles; cylinder, rectangle, circle, rectangle; cone, triangle, circle, triangle; prism, triangle and rectangles; pyramid, triangles and a square with diagonals

hold_back: Cube: squares; cuboid: rectangles; parallelepiped: parallelogram and rectangles; cylinder: rectangle, circle, rectangle; cone: triangle, circle, triangle; prism: triangle and rectangles; pyramid: triangles and a square with diagonals
maths_rules: views are listed as front, top, side
cube on a face: square, square, square
cuboid on a face: rectangle, rectangle, rectangle
parallelepiped leaning forward: front a rectangle, top a rectangle, side a parallelogram
cylinder standing: front a rectangle, top a circle, side a rectangle
cone standing on its base: front a triangle, top a circle with a dot at its centre, side a triangle
triangular prism with its triangle facing front: front a triangle, top a rectangle, side a rectangle
square pyramid standing on its base: front a triangle, top a square with both diagonals, side a triangle
check: the cube, cylinder, cone and square pyramid look the same from the front and from the side, so those two views match
video_script.design: One idea: the method of the worked cylinder, repeated for each solid. Each solid stands on the stage in turn; an eye moves to the front, above and the side, and the three outlines fill three frames.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about seven solids.
<bookmark mark='row'/>They are a cube, a cuboid, a parallelepiped, a cylinder, a cone, a prism and a pyramid.
<bookmark mark='para'/>A parallelepiped means a leaning box whose faces are parallelograms.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>A view means the flat picture you see looking straight at a solid from one direction. Find the front, top and side views of each.

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>We use the same method as for the cylinder in the example.
<bookmark mark='stand'/>First fix how each solid stands, on a face or on its base.
<bookmark mark='eye'/>Then look at it from the front, from above and from the side.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: cube on a face: three squares; cuboid on a face: three rectangles

narration: <bookmark mark='cube'/>Step one, the cube on a face. Every face is a square, so all three views are squares.
<bookmark mark='cuboid'/>The cuboid on a face has three views that are all rectangles.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: parallelepiped leaning forward: a parallelogram from the side; rectangles from the front and the top

narration: <bookmark mark='lean'/>Step two, the parallelepiped leaning forward. From the side we see a parallelogram.
<bookmark mark='rect'/>From the front and from above we see rectangles.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: cylinder standing: rectangle, circle, rectangle; cone standing: triangle, circle with a dot at its centre, triangle

narration: <bookmark mark='cyl'/>Step three, the cylinder standing up. The front is a rectangle, the top is a circle, and the side is a rectangle.
<bookmark mark='cone'/>The cone standing on its base shows a triangle from the front and the side. From above it shows a circle with a dot at its centre.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: triangular prism with its triangle facing front: a triangle, then two rectangles; square pyramid standing: triangles from the front and side, a square with both diagonals from the top

marks.diag: the four slanting edges meet above the centre and show as both diagonals of the square

narration: <bookmark mark='prism'/>Step four, the triangular prism with its triangle facing front. We see a triangle from the front, and rectangles from the top and the side.
<bookmark mark='pyr'/>The square pyramid standing on its base shows triangles from the front and the side.
<bookmark mark='diag'/>From above it shows a square. The four slanting edges meet above the centre, so both diagonals show.

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>Step five, check the front and side views. The cube, cylinder, cone and square pyramid look the same from both, so their two views match.
<bookmark mark='differ'/>The cuboid is longer one way, so its front and side rectangles differ.
